lessons.title: Asking a question
lessons.objective: Asking a question: Poser une question asks for information, while demander quelque chose asks for an item, an action or a favor.
lessons.explanation:
Poser une question asks for information, while demander quelque chose asks for an item, an action or a favor. Demander à quelqu'un introduces the person asked; demander si, où or quand opens an indirect question, and se renseigner means ask for information.

lessons.title: Taking, drinking and choosing transport
lessons.objective: Taking, drinking and choosing transport: Prendre has several everyday meanings.
lessons.explanation:
Prendre has several everyday meanings. Prendre le bus means take the bus; prendre un café means have a coffee; prendre une décision means make a decision. It is irregular: je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent, with the participle pris.

D'abord, j'ai cherché la bonne sortie. — First I looked for the correct exit.

lessons.title: Waiting and hoping
lessons.objective: Waiting and hoping: Attendre quelqu'un or attendre quelque chose means wait for a person or thing, with no preposition after the verb.
lessons.explanation:
Attendre quelqu'un or attendre quelque chose means wait for a person or thing, with no preposition after the verb. lessons.title: Putting, throwing and fixed phrases
lessons.objective: Putting, throwing and fixed phrases: Jeter means throw (away) and doubles the t before a silent ending: je jette, but nous jetons.
lessons.explanation:
Jeter means throw (away) and doubles the t before a silent ending: je jette, but nous jetons. French uses a separate verb for each kitchen action (mettre du sel = put in salt, ajouter = add, verser = pour), and some fixed phrases must be learned whole: jeter un coup d'œil means take a look, and manquer à means miss someone (Ma grand-mère me manque). Do not apply one English gloss everywhere.
Il y a trop de sel dans la soupe. — There is too much salt in the soup.
Nous avons peu de légumes frais. — We have few fresh vegetables.

lessons.title: Opening and available hours
lessons.objective: Opening and available hours: Ouvrir is an -ir verb with -er endings in the present (j'ouvre, tu ouvres) and has the irregular participle ouvert.
lessons.explanation:
Ouvrir is an -ir verb with -er endings in the present (j'ouvre, tu ouvres) and has the irregular participle ouvert. Être ouvert describes a state (la porte est ouverte); j'ai ouvert, with avoir, describes a completed action.

Léa a mis les dossiers sur la table. — Léa has put the folders on the table.

Envoyer means send something (envoyer quelque chose à quelqu'un): j'envoie, nous envoyons, future j'enverrai. Faire + infinitive means have something done or order an action, as in a fait vérifier le lien. Envoyer quelqu'un quelque part sends a person there, and an order with faire + infinitive may sound stronger than demander de.
J'ai écrit à Margaux ce matin. — I wrote to Margaux this morning.
Je lui ai expliqué le changement d'horaire. — I explained the schedule change to her.

lessons.title: Remembering and reminding
lessons.objective: Remembering and reminding: Se rappeler quelque chose means remember something, with no de before the object.
lessons.explanation:
Se rappeler quelque chose means remember something, with no de before the object. Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un means remind someone, and the l doubles before a silent ending: je me rappelle, but nous nous rappelons. Unlike se souvenir de, se rappeler normally takes no de before its direct object.
Avant, nous habitions près de la rivière. — We used to live near the river.
Notre maison avait une petite cour. — Our house had a small courtyard.

Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un means remind someone, and the l doubles before a silent ending: je me rappelle, but nous nous rappelons. Unlike se souvenir de, se rappeler normally takes no de before its direct object. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

items.note: The final -ls is silent: gentils is said "zhahn-tee".
Près has a grave accent and sounds like "preh"; the s is silent.
Feminine. Elision: la école becomes l'école.
